title: Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery: Order of Application When a Debtor Owes More Than One Debt
content:
When a debtor has more than one debt open for collection in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery**, an amount withheld from one benefit payment is applied first to the debt with the earliest notice date, and only the remainder passes to the next debt in that order; debts on hold are skipped. A direct payment the debtor designates for a specific debt is applied to that debt; an undesignated direct payment follows the same earliest-notice order. Within one debt, a collection is applied in the order of application set for its debt type, so interest accrued is paid before principal on an interest-bearing debt.

**Total amount owed.** The amount a debtor is quoted as their total amount owed is the combined open balance across all the debtor's debts: the sum of the balances of every debt whose status is active, on hold, in a repayment plan or referred to Treasury. Debts paid in full, waived or compromised are not part of it.

## Condition — result

| Money received | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Amount withheld from one benefit payment | Earliest-notice debt first, the remainder to the next debt in notice-date order; debts on hold skipped |
| Direct payment designated for a specific debt | That debt |
| Direct payment with no designation | Earliest-notice order, as for an offset |
| Any amount reaching an interest-bearing debt | Accrued interest first, then principal |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A debtor owes an education overpayment noticed in March with 150.00 USD left, a pension overpayment noticed in May with 900.00 USD left, and a compensation overpayment noticed in January that is on hold. A benefit offset of 400.00 USD skips the on-hold debt, pays the March debt's 150.00 USD in full, and applies the remaining 250.00 USD to the May debt, leaving 650.00 USD there.

The total amount owed quoted to this debtor includes all three balances, the on-hold debt among them, because an on-hold debt is still open.
